title: A Watch at Dusk
author: Miriam Vale
pages: I kept the bakery open for the names on his list. At dusk we sat together. The ticking passed our window and went on down the road.
In that round room, one glass case shone before his hand moved. I threw my pan at the shining glass. For a moment he was the one afraid.

title: Glass That Fed It
author: Elias Venn
pages: Three skulls. Four blocks of soul sand. We expected a monster. Its own ribs swallowed it and left a doorway. We should have left then.
The doorway inside was still there. I crawled back through it. The others kept shooting from the shelter; the thing did not even flinch.
One glass anchor lit before its chest opened. A skull hit that glass and the light ran backward into the beast. Wait for the glass to shine. My hands will not stop

title: The Eye That Waited
author: Nessa Ward
pages: Twelve eyes, no doorway. I stood on the frame and reached into the dark with my gift. It was like holding a breath through my hands. It took everything.
One eye kept my light while I rested. Not long. I stood on the eye beside it, on the same straight edge, and tried again. The two lights found each other.

title: Under a Violet Sky
author: Owen Pike
pages: We followed the beam down from the dragon's crystal to a glass focus. There was a plate to stand on. My gift answered when I faced the glass and held it there.
When the feed broke, the dragon came down. That was our chance. The low wave could be jumped. Its long lines stayed where they first appeared; we moved sideways.

title: The Bell Kept Ringing
author: Sela Moss
pages: I knew the miller before his hands caught fire. The circle formed under me, then stayed there when I ran. The flames hit the place I had been.
After his great burst he bent double. Kit waited for that moment to strike. I took the children past the well. Someone has to move the people, too.

title: Nine Quiet Footsteps
author: Arun Bellamy
pages: The grey coat walked beside the prisoner. Wherever he went, my sparks died. Hiding behind a wall did nothing. Backing away let them return.
We drew the others off. I stayed beyond his quiet and struck the grey coat first. The prisoner's hands lit before the man reached the ground.
